images.name: 청월 삼중 유영
images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one NEW full-length legendary fantasy longbow concept illustration at 1024x1536 portrait. Both input pictures are DESIGN REFERENCES ONLY: reference 1 is A04, with elegant branching moon antlers; reference 2 is A05, with beautiful overlapping physical blue crescent moon pieces. Output ONLY one new bow, no reference collage or comparison. The design family is "Twilight of the Blue Moon", noble clear blue beauty: the body itself is luminous sapphire, deep cobalt moonstone and clear blue moonlit glass, with very fine restrained gold filigree edging and supports. Preserve the references' refined blue crystalline material, elegant soft curves, decorative craftsmanship, physical moon symbols, airy negative spaces and impressive asymmetry. Do not turn it into steel, grey metal, painted blue iron or a huge solid circular lump. Exactly ONE bow upright in a near-front view with only a slight three-quarter turn; the entire bow fits within the canvas with 5% empty margin around ALL tips, curving protrusions and the string. Tall weapon large in frame with high readable detail, 90% canvas height. Clear functional grip, two continuous functional recurved limbs, and ONE taut fine continuous bowstring visibly connected to the upper and lower tips on the right. Strong structural upper-versus-lower asymmetry in limb length, mass, curves and ornaments; absolutely no mirrored upper and lower halves. Solid almost-black midnight navy background, quiet polished studio concept-art lighting, blue translucent edges, restrained internal moonlight, no floating aura that hides silhouette. Full lower tip must be visible. No people, hands, arrows, swords, second bow, second view, inset, text, labels or watermark.

Specific new design:
A05-dominant variation. Design a graceful upper-heavy bow with THREE clearly separated, partly overlapping physical blue crescent moons flowing diagonally upward from the left of the grip, attached into a delicate continuous gold-veined blue limb. Each crescent has a noticeably different tilt: the largest long narrow crescent high above the grip opens upper-right, the medium crescent extends left and opens right-up at a flatter angle, the smallest near the grip opens almost upward. Three different sizes, with generous beautiful empty spaces between the thin horns. Their arrangement forms one broad airy rising sweep rather than a vertical necklace. Use a relatively low grip and a long slender upper recurved limb that sweeps around the crescents. The lower limb is shorter, very slim and smooth with a single elegant small reverse hook, no moons duplicated below. Three crescents are the unmistakable dominant silhouette.
